critical_code_review_comments: BUG (now fixed): /app/backend/client_delivery.py previously defined `class FounderReplyReq(_Auth)` inside the `make_client_delivery_router` factory function. FastAPI's dependency/body resolver only recognises Pydantic models referenced from module-level scope when wiring POST bodies — a locally-defined class was treated as an unknown type and FastAPI fell back to treating `payload` as a query-string parameter, so every /api/client/reply POST returned 422. Fix: moved FounderReplyReq to module level beside the other request models.

/app/backend/client_delivery.py _sync_status_from_tasks uses `done < total // 2` for in_progress and `done < total` for review — with 6 tasks that means 1–2 done → in_progress, 3–5 done → review, 6 → completed. Matches spec.
client_token is correctly stripped from all founder-facing responses via _strip_token; public portal responses only return the client fields (no token leak).
Magic link URL uses SITE_URL env correctly; falls back to https://creatorboostai.com if unset.

Upload endpoint enforces 5 MB cap via raw-bytes length check on decoded base64 — correct. Returns 413 with a clear message. /api/client/portal/upload correctly omits content_b64 from the echoed response.
Avatar surface='client_portal' correctly forces role='delivery' in /app/backend/avatar.py line 446-447 regardless of user-message keywords — prevents accidental upsell in the client portal.
ops_center.py /leads/status correctly wraps the auto_onboard call in try/except so a client-onboarding failure does NOT block the lead-status update. Good defensive pattern.
client_delivery.py is 566 lines — single file is borderline. If Iter 56 extends this module, consider splitting public vs founder endpoints into two routers.

rca of the issue: Root cause for the /api/client/reply 422: In FastAPI, when a path-operation function's body parameter is annotated with a Pydantic BaseModel that is defined inside a closure (here, inside make_client_delivery_router), FastAPI's body detection (which uses get_type_hints and isinstance checks against pydantic.BaseModel at route-registration time) can succeed BUT the signature's annotation is looked up via typing.get_type_hints with the module's globalns, and a locally-scoped class that happens to share a name with no global binding is sometimes unresolved, causing FastAPI to fall back to query-param treatment. The fix — hoisting FounderReplyReq to module scope alongside the other request models — makes the class resolvable from client_delivery's module globals and FastAPI correctly treats `payload` as a request body. Reproduction: POST /api/client/reply with full JSON body → 422 `missing query.payload`. Mitigation (permanent): module-level Pydantic models only.
